title: Power drawn by a circulating pump
intro:
A test rig ran a circulating pump at 16 operating points. At each it recorded the flow (L/s), the head (m), the temperature of the water (°C) and the electrical power drawn (kW). Fit Power = b₀ + b₁·Flow + b₂·Head + b₃·Water temp by least squares and judge the fit.

Find R², adjusted R², the overall F statistic and its error degrees of freedom. Give R² and adjusted R² to four decimals, F to two decimals; the degrees of freedom are a whole number.

To use the Workbench: press **Copy the data**, press Ctrl+B, click **+ Data table** and paste (Ctrl+V). Choose **Multiple regression**, set **Data table** to the table you pasted, **Response column (y)** to *Power*, **Predictor columns** to *Flow, Head, Water temp* and **Variable selection** to *All the predictors listed*. Ctrl+L brings you back.

RSquared.says: That is adjusted R². R² itself is 1 − SS_E/SS_T, with no charge for the number of predictors.

AdjustedRSquared.says: That is R². Adjusted R² charges for the predictors: 1 − (1 − R²)(n − 1)/(n − k − 1).
You divided by n − k = 13. The error degrees of freedom are n − k − 1: the intercept is a coefficient too.

DfError.says: n − k = 13 forgets the intercept. Four coefficients are estimated (b₀ to b₃), so the error degrees of freedom are n − k − 1.
n − 1 = 15 is the total degrees of freedom. Subtract the k = 3 degrees of freedom of the regression as well.

hints: All three predictors go into one model; n = 16 operating points and k = 3 predictors.
F = (R²/k) / [(1 − R²)/(n − k − 1)], the same as MS_R/MS_E, with k and n − k − 1 degrees of freedom.
